column3: Description
Type or category of the SC node (e.g., manufacturer, distributor)
Geographic location (latitude, longitude) of the node
Whether the node has inventory storage capability
Type of inventory (e.g., finished goods, raw materials)
List of products that are stored in the inventory
Time for which a perishable product stays usable at the node before it expires, or the rate at which it spoils
Replenishment policy (e.g., periodic, economic order quantity)
Maximum inventory level that can be stored
Inventory on hand plus inventory on order or in transit, minus backlog, tracked during the simulation and compared with the reorder point by reorder-point policies
Threshold to trigger replenishment
Target level to which inventory is raised when a replenishment order is placed
Quantity ordered or produced per replenishment order or production run
Buffer stock held to absorb demand and lead time variability
Service level or fill rate a policy is set to reach, such as a 95% fill rate used to size safety stock (an input, unlike the measured customer service level)
Time interval for placing replenishment orders
Number of periods the node's planning or replenishment logic looks ahead when it sets orders or production, fixed or rolled forward, including any frozen part
Forecast of the demand the node faces, with its error or bias, used to set orders and plans
Cost incurred per unit for holding inventory
Cost of operating the storage facility, such as refrigerated storage in cold chains
Cost incurred per order placed to the supplier to replenish the inventory
Price paid to the supplier per unit bought, including premiums for emergency or urgent purchases (the fixed cost of placing an order is Order Cost)
Penalty cost for delayed orders
Whether demand the node cannot fill is backordered and filled later or lost, with any limit on it and any backlog at the start of a run
Decrease in product value over time due to wear, tear, or unfavorable market conditions
Cost of setting up the node (building the production plant or warehouse)
Price at which the node sells a unit of product, including markdowns
Type, timing, frequency, or probability of an event that makes this node unavailable or reduces its capacity, such as a facility closure, supply disruption, or equipment failure
Time for which the node remains unavailable or at reduced capacity after a disruption, including repair time
Time taken by the node to resume normal operation after a disruption
Cost incurred per disruption at this node, including the cost of recovery
Number of alternative suppliers or supply regions the node can draw on when its main source fails
Cost to produce a unit or batch of product (node-specific attribute: production nodes)
Maximum quantity the node can produce per unit of time (node-specific attribute: production nodes)
Share of the output or of the received supply that is good, defective, rejected, or scrapped
Rate at which trucks, trains, or vessels arrive at the node (node-specific attribute: ports and terminals)
Time to process, handle, load, or unload a unit or vehicle at the node (node-specific attribute: production and handling nodes)

Time from the release of a production order to its completion, including the planned lead times of MRP and the decoupled lead times of demand-driven MRP, unlike the transport lead time on a link (node-specific attribute: production nodes)
Number of workers, machines, or handling equipment that serve flow at the node, and their shifts or operating hours (node-specific attribute: production and handling nodes)

Rule by which the node decides which order, job or vehicle is served next, where goods are stored or picked, or how scarce stock is allocated (for example first-in-first-out, earliest due date, first-expires-first-out, priority or rationing, storage assignment, picker routing)
Interval in which the node accepts a delivery, pickup or visit, such as a customer's delivery window or an appointment slot at a terminal
Description
Number of product units sold per unit of time (day, month, or quarter)
Total number of items sold over a given time period
Net profit generated over a given time period (current month/quarter) or per time unit
Inventory levels at regular time intervals (daily or monthly)
Number of times the inventory is sold and replaced in a period, such as annual sales divided by average inventory
Number of orders (and product quantity) placed by this node
Number of orders (and product quantity) received at this node
Number of orders fulfilled by this node
Percentage of demand fulfilled
Number of orders not fulfilled by this node due to unavailability
Inventory waste due to product expiration (applicable for perishable products)
Quantity of goods produced in a given time period
Probability of reliable supply at the node
Node's ability to recover from disruption
Quantity of demand not met by this node
Quantity of accepted orders not yet fulfilled, carried over and filled later rather than lost
Time that vehicles, containers, or orders spend waiting or being handled at the node, such as dwell or turnaround time
Share of time that equipment, vehicles, or staff at the node are busy
Distance or time that pickers, robots, or automated guided vehicles travel inside the node (node-specific attribute: warehouses)
